Modify columns of an existing level, or of the rows in hand

Source: R/levels.R
modify_level.Rd

Adds or overwrites columns, as dplyr::mutate does. Named after a level that already exists, it works at that level: the expressions are evaluated once per unit of the level, N is the number of units, and the result is written back to every row of each unit. Left unnamed, it works on the rows in hand, with an optional .by for split-apply-combine on a grouping column.

Usage

modify_level(..., .by = NULL)

Arguments

...

Column expressions to add or overwrite.

.by

Optional character string: column name to group by before evaluating expressions.

Value

A fabricatr_level object, meaningful only as a named or unnamed argument to fabricate. It adds or overwrites columns and changes no rows: the frame it returns has the same number of rows as the one it received.

Details

On a flat frame, unnamed modify_level(..., .by = "g") gives the same columns as group_by(g) |> mutate(...) |> ungroup(). Its use is that it runs inside the fabricate() call, so it is part of a DeclareDesign declare_model() step rather than a pipe after it, and that only it can work at a named level.

Which columns a level can see

Inside regions = modify_level(...), the columns in view are the ones that take a single value per region: those built at the regions level or above it. A column built at a level nested inside regions varies within a region, so it is out of view, as it is in fabricatr 1.x. To summarise such a column per region, leave the level name off and group instead: modify_level(mean_b = mean(b), .by = "regions").

Examples

# At a named level: one draw per region, written to every city in it
fabricate(
  regions = add_level(N = 3, a = 1:3),
  cities  = add_level(N = 2, b = rnorm(N)),
  regions = modify_level(z = rnorm(N), a2 = a * 2)
)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>   regions     a cities       b      z    a2
#>   <chr>   <int> <chr>    <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 1           1 1       0.172   1.12      2
#> 2 1           1 2       1.72    1.12      2
#> 3 2           2 3       0.546  -1.46      4
#> 4 2           2 4      -0.107  -1.46      4
#> 5 3           3 5      -0.0303 -0.296     6
#> 6 3           3 6      -0.666  -0.296     6

# On the rows in hand, grouped
fabricate(
  N = 50,
  cluster = sample(1:5, N, replace = TRUE),
  Y = rnorm(N),
  modify_level(cluster_mean = mean(Y), .by = "cluster")
)
#> # A tibble: 50 × 4
#>    ID    cluster      Y cluster_mean
#>    <chr>   <int>  <dbl>        <dbl>
#>  1 01          2  0.162      -0.0480
#>  2 02          4 -0.196       0.188 
#>  3 03          2 -0.412      -0.0480
#>  4 04          2 -0.847      -0.0480
#>  5 05          4 -0.620       0.188 
#>  6 06          3  0.455       0.265 
#>  7 07          4 -0.313       0.188 
#>  8 08          5  1.28       -0.352 
#>  9 09          1 -0.619       0.362 
#> 10 10          2  0.253      -0.0480
#> # ℹ 40 more rows
